(By Sri.P.Ramakrishna,

 (By Sri.B.R.Venkatesh Kamath,

 JUDGMENT

This is the Petition filed by the Petitioners under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation SCCH24 of Rs.50,00,000/ for the Death of one Sudarashana in a road traffic accident dated 11.05.2021.
2.

The case of the Petitioners in brief is that, on 11.05.2021 at about 1.30 p.m., the deceased Sudarshana was riding his Deo motorcycle bearing Regn.KA11EN 5711 to bring lunch from the hotel at Thalaghattapura, when he reached near Jnanasweekar School and took right turn at that juncture another motorcycle bearing reg.No.KA05KK7272 came in a rash and negligent manner without observing any of the traffic rules and regulations passing on the said road and dashed against the motorcycle of the deceased and caused the accident, due to impact the deceased sustained severed head injury and other injuries all over the body and immediately the deceased was shifted to NIMHANS Hospital, wherein took series of xrays, scan and other treatment and then shifted to Sanjay Gandhi Hospital, Bangalore, for further treatment on the same day and during the course of SCCH24 treatment, he succumbed to the said injuries on 16.05.2021.

Thereafter the body was shifted to KIMS Hospital and Research Center wherein conducted postmortem on 17.05.2021 and handed over the body to them and they took the body to their native place in a Ambulance with a freezer box and for the same they have incurred a sum of Rs.1,00,000/ and performed final rites by spending Rs.2,00,000/.
3.

It is further case of the Petitioners that, the deceased was hale and healthy and was working as cashier in India Oil Petrol Bunk, Talaghattapura, near NICE road, Bengaluru and earning a sum of Rs.25,000/ per month.
Due to his untimely death they have put to untold misery and mental agony, hardship and financial loss.
The Kumaraswamy Layout Traffic Police station have registered a case in Crime No.48/2021 u/Sec.279, 337 304(A) and 338 of IPC.
The 1st respondent being the RC owner and the 2nd respondent is the insurer of the SCCH24 offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to them.
4. In response to the summons issued by this court, the Respondents have appeared through their respective counsel and filed separate written statements.

Sri.Basavaraju vs Sri.Chandra D on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/176126049/
2 5.

The Respondent No.1 in his objections has denied the averments made in columns No.1 to 14A and 17 to 21 of the petition as they are not within his knowledge and also denied the averments made in column No.22 and submitted that his motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA05KK 7272 is insured with the second respondent and valid from 27.07.2020 to 26.07.2021 and also the driver of the motorcycle had possessed valid driving license and hence the respondent No.2 is liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
Accordingly prayed for dismissal of the petition against him.
SCCH24 6.

The Respondent No.2 in its written statement denied the case of the petitioners as false, admitted issuance of policy but their liability if any is subject to terms and conditions therein and submitted that there is non compliance of Section 134(c) and Section 158(6) of M.V. Act.
Further submitted that the rider of the offending vehicle had no valid DL, vehicle had no valid documents and hence there is contravention of policy terms and conditions.
Therefore, prayed for dismissal of the petition against them.

7. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues are framed:
1.
Whether the Petitioners prove that, they are the only legal representatives of deceased 'Sudarshana S/o Basavaraju' and were dependent on him ?

2. Whether the Petitioners prove that, the deceased succumbed to the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 11.05.2021 at about 01.30 p.m., near Jnanasweekara School, Talaghattapura, Kanakapura main road,
Bengaluru, due to the actionable SCCH24 negligence of the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA05KK7272 ?
3. Whether the Petitioners are entitled for compensation? If so, what is the quantum?
From whom?
4.

What Order or Award?
8.

In order to prove their case, the Petitioners have examined the Petitioner No.2 - Smt.Nanjamani  mother of the deceased as PW.1 and got marked 14 documents as per Exs.P.1 to P.14 and also examined Mr.Chethan eye witness of the accident as PW.2 and got marked documents as per Exs.P15 and P16.
On the other side, the Respondents did not examine any witness nor produced any documents on their behalf.

With consent the true copies of spot sketch and policy are got marked as Exs.R1 and R2.
9.
Heard arguments of both Counsel and perused the materials on record.

SCCH24 Sri.Basavaraju vs Sri.Chandra D on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/176126049/
3 10.

My findings to the above issues are as follows: Issue No.1 : In the affirmative, Issue No.2 :
Partly in the affirmative, Issue No.3 : Partly in the affirmative, Issue No.4 : As per final order, for the following:
REASONS 11. ISSUE No.1: It is the case of the Petitioners that, the Petitioner No.1 and 2 are the parents and petitioner No.3 and 4 are sisters of the deceased - Sudarshana.
The Petitioners to prove this relationship have examined the second Petitioner as PW.1.
The PW.1 has specifically deposed this relationship in her chiefexamination.

Apart from that, to prove the relationship she has also produced notarized copies of DL of the deceased and Aadhar cards of the petitioners and also produced the SSLC marks card of the deceased and copy of provisional National Trade certificate of deceased as per Exs.P.11 to P14 which are SCCH24 the public documents and have got presumptive value under law.

In the DL of the deceased his father's name is mentioned as Basavaraju, who is the Petitioner No.1, in the Aadhar card of the Petitioner No.1 his father's name is mentioned as Siddegowda, in the Aadhar card of the Petitioner No.2 her husband's name is mentioned as Basavaraju, in the Aadhar card of the petitioner No.3 her husband's name is mentioned as D.B.Basavaraju, R/at #422, C.A Kere Hobli Devegowdanadoddi village, Menasagere, Menasagere Maddur Mandya, Karnataka 571422 and in the Aadhar card of the petitioner No.4 her father's name is mentioned as Basavaraju.
These documents have not been seriously disputed by the Respondents.
The Respondents have not produced any contrary documents on record.

As such,
there are no reasons to discard the oral and documentary evidence produced by the Petitioners.

Under such circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 and documents SCCH24 produced this court is of the opinion that the Petitioners 1 and 2 are the parents and petitioner No.3 and 4 are the sisters of the deceased Sudarshana.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is held in the Affirmative.
12. ISSUE No.2:

The Petitioners to prove that the accident was occurred due the actionable negligence on part of the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA05KK7272 have examined the Petitioner No.2/mother of the deceased as PW.1 and produced 8 documents as per Exs.P.1 to P.8.

The PW.1 has specifically deposed in her evidence that her son Sudarshana was riding his Deo motorcycle bearing Regn.KA11EN5711 to bring the lunch from the hotel at Thalaghattapura,
when he reached near Jnanasweekar School at took right turn at that juncture another motorcycle bearing reg.No.KA05KK7272 came in a rash and negligent manner without observing any of the traffic SCCH24 rules and regulations passing on the said road and dashed against the motorcycle of the deceased and caused the accident, due to impact the deceased sustained severed head injury and succumbed to the said injuries during the treatment.

On the other side, the Respondents have denied the case of the petitioners and the respondent No.2 specifically denied the rash and negligence of the rider of the offending vehicle and also contended that there was negligence on the part of the rider of the deceased himself.
In support of their defence the Respondents have not examined any witness nor produced any documents.
In the crossexamination of PW.1 nothing worth is elicited.

13. The petitioners have got examined the eyewitness as PW.2 who has deposed in support of the case of the petitioners with regard to alleged manner of accident and he witnessing the said Sri.Basavaraju vs Sri.Chandra D on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/176126049/
4 accident.

In the cross examination it is elicited that the accident spot is SCCH24 Bangalore Kananakapura road, the accident occurred in the circle, on the alleged date of accident there was lockdown due to covid 19 effect and nobody used to go outside, on that day the road empty/free, on that day the deceased was taking turn and the offending vehicle was coming in straight way, the accident occurred on the left side of the road.

14. Nodoubt the respondent no.2 has not lead any evidence in support of their defence but the counsel for the respondent no.2 points out on the Ex.R1/Spot sketch and contended that the accident took place in the middle of the road and hence there was negligence on the part of the deceased but the petitioners have not produced the said spot sketch only to suppress the real facts and hence prayed to consider and appreciate the Ex.R1.
The PW.2 has denied that the accident took place in the middle of road and also denied the correctness of the Ex.R1/spot sketch.

Mere denial of Ex.R1 which has got initial SCCH24 presumptive value under law and as the petitioners rely upon the police documents the duty cast upon them to produce the spot sketch but they have not produce the said document thinking that if produce would go against them and the real fact of negligence on the part of the deceased comes to picture.

When the document/Ex.R1 drawn by the I.O. during the course of investigation itself clearly shows that the accident occurred in the middle of the road then there is no need for the respondent no.2 to lead separate evidence to prove the negligence on the part of the deceased.
The PW.2 clearly stated that it was a lockdown period and vehicles were not plying on that day and the deceased was taking turn.

Further the Ex.R1 clearly shows that the deceased was crossing the road and was proceedings towards Judicial Layout road, from this it is clear that the deceased without observing the movements of on coming vehicle had took turn in a negligent manner and appears to have not worn the SCCH24 helmet and contributed to the accident.

Therefore, there was a contributed negligence on the part of the deceased in causing the accident and nodoubt the rider of the offending vehicle also should have taken care to avoid the accident and as he was also riding his bike in a rash and negligent manner without observing the deceased caused the accident and therefore, the contributory negligence on the part of the deceased needs to assessed at 25% and rest of the negligence is on the part of the rider of the offending vehicle.
15.
Therefore, on appreciating the documents on record and the evidence this Tribunal has drawn the conclusion as above.
The PM report clearly show that the deceased died due to effect of HEAD INJURY SUSTAINED".

Under these circumstances, this court is of the opinion that the rider of the offending motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA05KK7272 ridden it in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endangering to human life and SCCH24 dashed to the vehicle of the deceased and there was also contributory negligence on the part of the deceased which lead to the accident, result of which deceased Sudarshana had sustained injuries and succumbed to the injuries.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 is partly in the affirmative.
16. ISSUE No. 3:

The PW.1 has specifically deposed before this court that due to the untimely death of the deceased, they have lost the bread earner of their family and their loved one and further stated that due to the accidental injuries their son deceased Sudarshana died during the treatment and PM was done and later the cremation was conducted.

This court while discussing the issue No.2 has come to the conclusion that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligence of the rider of Sri.Basavaraju vs Sri.Chandra D on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/176126049/
5 the offending motorcycle alongwith the contributory negligence on the part of the SCCH24 deceased.
Under such circumstances, the petitioners are entitled for compensation.

Monthly income:
17.

According to the Petitioners the deceased was working as cashier in Indian Oil Petrol bunk and earning sum of Rs.25,000/ per month but have not produced any relevant documents nor got examined the employer.
In the absence of specific evidence for proof of income, the version of the Petitioners that the deceased was earning Rs.25,000/ per month is not acceptable.
Under such circumstances, this court has to consider the income of the deceased notionally for calculating the compensation.
At the time of accident the deceased was a young aged person aged 26 years as could be make out from Ex.P.11/SSLC marks card which shows the date of birth of the deceased is 19.04.1995.

Though the Ex.P.13/DL of the deceased shows that the date of birth of deceased is 19.04.1991 but the SSLC marks card being document SCCH24 came into existence prior to Ex.P13 and hence Ex.P11 is considered.
The accident took place on 11.05.2021.
Considering the said dates it is clear that the deceased was completed the age of 26 on 10.04.2021 itself and hence he was aged about 26 years as on the date of accident.

Therefore, having regard to the age of the deceased, and also relying on the decision of Hon'ble H.C. in the case of Sumangala & Others and Ramanagouda &
Anr., in MFA No:202534/2019(MVC) wherein the notified notional income chart of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority is considered for fixing the notional income and accordingly the monthly notional income of the deceased is considered as Rs.15,000/ per month.
Age of the deceased:
18.
In so far as age of the deceased is concerned, as discussed above the notarized copy of SSLC marks card of the deceased as per Ex.P.11 is considered.
As such his SCCH24 age was 26 years as on the date of his death.
Therefore, the age of the deceased is considered 26 years.
i) LOSS OF DEPENDENCY
As per principles of law laid down in the case of Sarala Verma V/s Delhi Transport Corporation, appropriate multiplier applicable to his age is 17.

entities.text: Sarala Verma V/s Delhi Transport Corporation
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the instant case, the deceased has mother, father and sisters.

The PW.1 in his cross examination stated that the petitioner no.1 is doing coolie work and she also does coolie work, the third petitioner is married and 4 th petitioner is studying, but she denied that they were not depending on income of the deceased.
In absence of specific evidence that the petitioner no.2 was earning sufficiently she is only considered as dependent on the income of the deceased.

Further, it is relevant to note that as per the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in SCCH 24 special leave petition No. 25590/2014 between National Insurance Company Vs Pranay Sethi and others and other connected petitions, even in case of the death of self employed and fixed salary also, the Dependents are entitled for future prospects.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Vs Pranay Sethi and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, in the present case since the deceased is less than 40 years age, 40% future prospects have to be added to his monthly income.
However, as the deceased is a bachelor, as per the Sarala Verma's case, half of his income has to be deducted towards his personal and living expenses.

If 40% income is added to his monthly income,
Sri.Basavaraju vs Sri.Chandra D on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/176126049/
6
it comes around Rs.21,000/ (Rs.15,000/ + Rs.6,000/) and if 50% is deducted towards his living and personal expenses, balance comes to Rs.10,500/ (Rs.21,000/  Rs.10,500/).
Therefore, the total loss of dependency would be Rs.21,42,000/ (Rs.10,500/ X 12 X 17 = Rs.21,42,000/).
SCCH24 ii) TRANSPORTATION, MEDICAL AND FUNERAL EXPENSES

In so far as the funeral and transportation expenses are concerned, the Petitioners have pleaded that they have spent Rs.1,50,000/ towards towards transportation of dead body, funeral, obsequies and other incidental expenses.
No documents are produced in this regard.

However, looking into the facts and circumstances of the case, it is difficulty to maintain bills for transportation of dead body and funeral expenses and hence it would be appropriate to award compensation of Rs.20,000/ towards funeral and transportation expenses.
MEDICAL EXPENSES:

In so far as the medical expenses is concerned, the petitioner has contended that they have spent Rs.2,00,000/ towards Medical expenses of the deceased Sudarshana. who was treated at Sanjay Gandhi Hospital.
In this regard the petitioners have produced prescriptions SCCH24 and 12 medical bills for a sum of Rs.38,245/ as per Ex.P.9 and 10.
In the cross examination nothing worth is elicited and there is no contrary to these bills from the respondents.

Therefore, the Petitioners are entitled for a sum of Rs.38,245/
under this head.
iii) LOSS OF ESTATE:
As mentioned above, the deceased was earning a sum of Rs.15,000/ per month.
Out of this, he was getting  of his income towards personal expenses.
Such being the case, out of this, certainly he would have saved some amount and created estate in favour of the Petitioners.
Therefore, the Petitioners are entitled for a sum of Rs.20,000/ under the head of loss of estate.
(iv) LOSS OF CONSORTIUM:
The Petitioner Nos.1 and 2 are the parents of the deceased and petitioner No.3 and 4 is the sisters of the deceased.
They have lost their loving son and brother.
If SCCH24 he was alive he would taken care of them and given full love and affection to the Petitioners.
In Magma General Insurance company Limited the Hon'ble Apex court has considered the compensation under head of loss of consortium.

The Hon'ble Apex court in three judge Bench in United Indian Insurance Company Ltd. Vs.
Satinder Kaur @ Satvinder Kaur and others, (2020) SCC online 410, had reaffirmed the view of the two judge Bench in Magma General Insurance company Ltd.

entities.text:
United Indian Insurance Company Ltd. Vs.
Satinder Kaur @ Satvinder Kaur and others, (2020) SCC online 410
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In Paragraph 53 to 65, dealt with three conventional heads and discussed about "Consortium" to be a compendious term, which encompasses spousal consortium,
parental consortium, as well as filial consortium.
The right to consortium would include the company, care, help, comfort, guidance, solace and affection of the deceased, which is a loss to his family.
Filial Consortium - A child's society, affection and companionship given to a parent.

Therefore, the claimants are also entitled for Sri.Basavaraju vs Sri.Chandra D on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/176126049/
7 compensation under the SCCH24 head of consortium.
Therefore, the Petitioners are entitled a sum of Rs.1,60,000/ (Rs.40,000/ each) under this head.

As such, in total, the compensation comes to Rs.23,80,245/ and if negligence of the deceased as assessed at 25% needs to be deducted in the total compensation and if it is done then the remaining compensation comes to Rs.17,85,184/ (Rs.23,80,245/ 
Rs.5,95,061/) and if it rounded off it comes to Rs.17,85,200/ and hence the petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.17,85,200/ alongwith interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization.

Liability:
19.
As discussed above, the Respondent No.2  insurer has failed to prove its defence as contended except contributory negligence.
Under these circumstances, it is very clear that Respondents being the owner and the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally SCCH24 liable to pay the said compensation.
However, as the Petitioners have proved the existence of policy and its validity as on the date of accident, hence the insurer Respondent No.2 has got primary liability to satisfy the award.
The Petitioners have claimed an amount of Rs.50,00,000/, but they are entitled only for a sum of Rs.17,85,200/.
Therefore the Petition is liable to be allowed in part.
Accordingly I answer Issue No.3 is partly in the Affirmative.
20. ISSUE No.4:

In view of the findings of the above issue Nos.1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following:
[ ORDER
The Petition filed by the Petitioners under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part with cost.
SCCH24

The Petitioners are entitled for Compensation of Rs.17,85,200/ (Rupees Seventeen Lakhs Eighty Five Thousand and Two Hundred only) along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount.
The Respondents Nos.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.

However, as the policy existed the Respondent No.2 - insurer to indemnify respondent No.1 insured and is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest before this Tribunal within 60 days from the date of this Judgement.

On deposit of the award amount and interest, 20% shall be deposited in the name Sri.Basavaraju vs Sri.Chandra D on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/176126049/
8 SCCH24 of the Petitioner No.2 in any N/S bank for period of 3 years with a liberty to withdraw the periodical interest and in the balance amount a sum of Rs.40,000/
each shall be released in the name of the Petitioner No.1, 3 and 4 and the remaining entire balance amount to be released in favour of the petitioner No.2 on proper identification and due acknowledgment as per Rules.
The Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1000/.
Draw Award accordingly.

Considering the said dates it is clear that the deceased was completed the age of 26 on 10.04.2021 itself and hence he was aged about 26 years as on the date of accident.
Therefore, having regard to the age of the deceased, and also relying on the decision of Hon'ble H.C. in the case of Sumangala & Others and Ramanagouda &
Anr., in MFA No:202534/2019(MVC) wherein the notified notional income chart of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority is considered for fixing the notional income and accordingly the monthly notional income of the deceased is considered as Rs.15,000/ per month.
Age of the deceased:
18.
As such his SCCH24 age was 26 years as on the date of his death.
Therefore, the age of the deceased is considered 26 years.
As per principles of law laid down in the case of Sarala Verma V/s Delhi Transport Corporation, appropriate multiplier applicable to his age is 17.
In the instant case, the deceased has mother, father and sisters.
In absence of specific evidence that the petitioner no.2 was earning sufficiently she is only considered as dependent on the income of the deceased.
The Hon'ble Apex court in three judge Bench in United Indian Insurance Company Ltd. Vs.
Satinder Kaur @ Satvinder Kaur and others, (2020) SCC online 410, had reaffirmed the view of the two judge Bench in Magma General Insurance company Ltd.
However, as the Petitioners have proved the existence of policy and its validity as on the date of accident, hence the insurer Respondent No.2 has got primary liability to satisfy the award.

Therefore, the Petitioners are entitled a sum of Rs.1,60,000/ (Rs.40,000/ each) under this head.
The Petitioners have claimed an amount of Rs.50,00,000/, but they are entitled only for a sum of Rs.17,85,200/.
Therefore the Petition is liable to be allowed in part.
Accordingly I answer Issue No.3 is partly in the Affirmative.

In view of the findings of the above issue Nos.1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following:

The Petition filed by the Petitioners under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part with cost.

The Respondents Nos.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
However, as the policy existed the Respondent No.2 - insurer to indemnify respondent No.1 insured and is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest before this Tribunal within 60 days from the date of this Judgement.

8 SCCH24 of the Petitioner No.2 in any N/S bank for period of 3 years with a liberty to withdraw the periodical interest and in the balance amount a sum of Rs.40,000/
each shall be released in the name of the Petitioner No.1, 3 and 4 and the remaining entire balance amount to be released in favour of the petitioner No.2 on proper identification and due acknowledgment as per Rules.
The Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1000/.
Draw Award accordingly.
